label: Early original-phase input of l/g/a/n/q/b (positions 1-4)
explanation: Fires mostly during the original (input) phase at positions 1-4 (95% of activation mass is in the original phase, 91% at t=1..4), almost never at t=0, the delimiter step, or position 6 or later. Which token is being read matters a lot: l (rate 27%), g, a, n, q and b give the highest rates, with i/v/e weaker. Restricting to those six tokens at t=1..4 gives F1 about 0.48 on dev with mass recall about 0.65. Activation is higher on first occurrences of a token. The largest activations come in sequences that start with d (often d d / d p / d s followed by q/l/a/g), so the earlier context changes the magnitude. Weak residual firing (about 5% of mass) during the copy phase, roughly evenly spread over recall positions. The response depends on a token-by-context interaction that a simple predicate does not capture, so precision and recall are both incomplete.
